# Intro
[excited] Today: AWS flips on Graviton5 silicon, a16z launches an AI academy to replace your college degree, and a video paper that rewrites how models learn. Let's go.

---

# Story 1: AWS Graviton5 | EC2 R9g Instances Hit General Availability
### Landing Page
[confident] Amazon just shipped EC2 R9g and R9gd instances, powered by their new Graviton5 processors. That's the fifth generation of custom ARM silicon, now generally available for anyone to spin up.

### Demo
[amazed] Graviton5 pushes better performance-per-watt across the board, and the R9gd variant bolts on local NVMe storage. For memory-hungry workloads, that combo means fewer instances and a smaller cloud bill.

### Access
[excited] Both families are live in AWS regions right now, no waitlist. If you're running ARM-native containers, this is a drop-in upgrade worth benchmarking this week.

---

# Story 2: Video Cross-Attention | Closing the Modality Gap in Joint Video Generation
### Paper
[curious] Hugging Face paper twenty-six-oh-nine point two-seven-nine-oh-one. The claim: in joint multimodal diffusion transformers, every modality is equal — but video is more equal.

### Architecture
[confident] The authors find cross-attention asymmetry: audio and 3D motion develop strong mappings to video, but video doesn't reciprocate. They close that gap, sharpening joint generation quality across the stack.

### Release Horizon
[friendly] Open weights are flagged, five upvotes and climbing on the daily papers board. Early, but if you're building multimodal video, this is the architecture note to read now.

---

# Story 3: a16z AI Academy | An Alternative to the College Degree
### Headline
[skeptical] Andreessen Horowitz is launching an AI academy, positioned as a direct alternative to a four-year college degree. Three outlets confirmed it, so this isn't rumor.

### Evidence
[confident] The pitch is simple: ship real AI skills, skip the tuition and the debt. For a16z, it's talent pipeline plus brand — they get first look at the graduates they train.

### The Verdict
[curious] Whether an academy credential carries weight with hiring managers is the whole ballgame. Watch the first cohort's placement rates — that's the real scoreboard.

---

# Story 4: HappyWorld-Bench | Testing Whether Generated Worlds Stay Reliable
### Paper
[excited] HappyWorld-Bench, thirty-eight upvotes on Hugging Face. It's a benchmark that asks a harder question: not just how good a generated world looks, but whether it holds up when an agent pokes at it.

### Architecture
[amazed] Built on a hierarchical capability framework, it scores consistency and responsiveness under exploration, interaction, and modification. That's the gap between a pretty demo and a usable simulator.

### Release Horizon
[confident] Open weights flagged, and world models are the hottest research lane right now. If you're evaluating one, this benchmark just became your baseline.
